1.why: All five screens are static cards with no animations, carousels, or pop-up dialogs anywhere in the flow.

2.why: Each step has a bold dark heading and a single high-contrast primary button, though the large black 'Logs' panel competes visually with the real task.

3.why: Each screen holds only one short task, but the technical 'Logs (simulated delivery)' block occupies a third of the page and gives a non-technical user extra noise to filter out.

4.why: She must retain the 14-character composition rules, carry a 33-character recovery code and a separate six-digit code between screens, so several rules and steps must be held in mind.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: Nothing familiar is surfaced (no remembered email, no account name); the only pre-filled item is an opaque random recovery string that cannot be meaningfully recognised.

7.why: Sentences are short, plain-language, and rendered in a legible sans-serif with strong contrast, apart from the monospace log text.

8.why: No error state is shown in any screenshot — there is no visible validation message explaining a problem or how to correct it.

9.why: Fields have no placeholder examples or sample formats; the password rule is described in prose but no example password or code format is shown.

10.why: The password and code inputs are clearly labelled, but no alternative sign-in choices (face/biometric, magic link) are offered so 'choices' are minimal.

11.why: Every screen presents at most two buttons and one or two fields, so the user is never faced with many simultaneous options.

12.why: Step 5 shows 'Accepted securely' and the log records each stage, but outcomes such as the password being saved are only reported in the technical log, not in a clear user-facing confirmation.

13.why: Each card carries a one-line instruction and a repeated 'Stay safe' anti-phishing tip, but there are no task-specific help links, tooltips, or progress guidance for new steps.

14.why: A 'Start over' button exists on the verification step only; other steps offer no back or retry control, and no retry-after-error path is visible.

15.why: All five screens reuse the identical header, white rounded card, typography, button styling, and footer note, keeping the layout fully predictable.
